For the given environment, each of our ‘Demo Broadcasting’ users needs to be clean-slate wiped prior to the running of other automated tests. The objective here is to clear our certain UI and workflow elements that might otherwise confuse, complicate, or slow down automated/Agentic testing steps. # Clear Drafts ## If the active user has the ability to submit new requests they will have a Drafts folder in their navigation. On the Drafts page/folder view there is a ‘CLEAR ALL DRAFTS’ button in the upper right. ## Clicking this button will then ask for a confirmation, click ‘YES, DELETE’ and confirm the Drafts view has 0 spots/rows. # Notifications ## The ‘Bell’ icon that shows a user notifications in a small modal has a ‘VIEW ALL’ link at the bottom. ## After clicking ‘VIEW ALL’ there is a new slide-out shown which has a ‘Delete all' link in the upper right. ## Clicking this will ask for a confirmation, we want to click ‘YES, DELETE’ ## Confirm there are no notifications remaining # Tasks ## The ‘Clipboard’ icon that shows a user their assigned task/job assignments in a small drop-down modal also has a ‘VIEW ALL’ link that opens the full slide out. ## Confirm that the ‘Delete all’ for the Tasks also clears out all of the Task/Job assignment notifications from its unique slide-out. Once these tasks are completed for the full roster of ‘Demo Broadcasting’ users, the QA/2T environments are better prepared for automated testing of all product features. ---- Claude Generated Context: {noformat}Here is the complete Playwright context document: --- ## vProMedia Cart ID Playwright Test — DOM & Technical Reference ### 1. Entry URL ``` https://qa.vcreative.net/#/vpro/production-orders/folder/need-carts?user=600921 ``` - Hash-based Angular router (`#/vpro/...`) - `user=600921` is the specific Traffic Director user ID — hardcode this in the test - The folder slug `need-carts` is the custom saved search name (not an ID) - Sidebar nav label: `Need Carts (N)` where N counts remaining items --- ### 2. Framework & Architecture - **Angular** (standalone components, `_nghost-*` / `_ngcontent-*` attributes on all elements) - **PrimeNG** component library (p-datatable, p-paginator, p-confirmdialog, p-drawer, p-select) - **API base:** `https://vcapi-qa.vcreative.net` - **Lambda save endpoint:** `https://lambda.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/2015-03-31/functions/vAPI3_qa/invocations` - The app uses **polling** via `/auth/ssoRefresh` (fires every ~10s) to check lock states --- ### 3. Key Selectors #### Cart ID input (empty, needs filling) ```css input.po-text-cart-id[placeholder="---"] /* OR by generated ID pattern: */ input[id^="cart-id-input-"] /* When a spot has no cart, its input value is "" and placeholder is "---" */ ``` **HTML:** ```html ``` - The numeric suffix in the ID is the **spot ID** (e.g., `743850`) - The input lives inside: `app-vppo-cart-col > div > input` #### Row container ```css tr[app-vppo-spot-row] /* OR */ tr.p-datatable-selectable-row ``` **HTML attributes:** ```html ``` - Each data row is a `` with the `app-vppo-spot-row` directive attribute - The Cart ID `` within has class `po-col-cart-id` #### Scoping input to its row ```javascript // Get first empty cart ID input const input = document.querySelector('input.po-text-cart-id[placeholder="---"]'); // Get its containing row const row = input.closest('tr[app-vppo-spot-row]'); // Get spot ID from input's id attribute const spotId = input.id.replace('cart-id-input-', ''); ``` #### Table container ```css div#pn_id_1 /* PrimeNG datatable root */ table#pn_id_1-table tbody.p-datatable-tbody ``` --- ### 4. Lock State Elements When a cart ID is being edited, **sibling overlay `` elements** are injected into `tbody.p-datatable-tbody` immediately before each locked data row: ```html You are currently editing this spot You are currently editing another spot ``` **Playwright selectors for lock detection:** ```javascript // Wait for all locks to clear before proceeding: await expect(page.locator('tr.spot-edit-lock')).toHaveCount(0); // OR wait for the "another spot" locks to clear: await expect(page.locator('tr.spot-edit-lock:not(.locking-border-enable-editing)')).toHaveCount(0); ``` **Important:** The lock `` elements are DOM siblings of the data `` elements within the same `` — they are NOT children of the data rows. --- ### 5. The Save Flow (on blur/Tab) When the user tabs out of a cart ID input, the following network calls fire in order: | # | Method | Endpoint | Purpose | |---|--------|----------|---------| | 1 | POST | `/spots-locked` | Acquire lock: `{spotId, userId, timeStamp, lockedMessage, firmId, expireTime}` | | 2 | GET | `/spots/cartsInLastDays/{date}/{cartId}` | **Duplicate check** — verifies uniqueness | | 3 | POST | `lambda/.../vAPI3_qa` | **Actual save** — updates `vppo.spots` table with cart ID | | 4 | DELETE | `/spots-locked/{spotId}` | Release lock | | 5 | POST | `/user-spot-filter/processSpotUpdate/{spotId}` | Triggers filter refresh | | 6 | POST | `/spots/getDeltasAndPrepareSpotForLv/{spotId}` | Fetches updated spot data | | 7 | POST | `/auth/ssoRefresh` | Polls visible spot IDs and lock states | The row **disappears from the view** after step 5/6 when the filter determines the spot no longer matches "no Cart ID". --- ### 6. Validation Sidebar (Cart ID Range Check) If the entered value **fails validation** (must be 1000–9999), a sidebar panel opens instead of saving: ```css app-warningsidebar#warningSidebar /* Contains: */ app-v-sidebar#warning-v-sidebar ``` **Structure:** ```html
``` **The sidebar contains a second `input.po-text-cart-id`** for re-entering the cart ID. The Accept button is `disabled` until valid input is provided. **Playwright selectors:** ```javascript // Detect if validation sidebar is open: const sidebar = page.locator('#warningSidebar app-v-sidebar.p-drawer-active'); // Cancel and retry: await page.locator('#warningSidebar button.p-button-danger').click(); // Or fix value and accept: await page.locator('#warningSidebar input.po-text-cart-id').fill('2500'); await page.locator('#warningSidebar button.p-button:not(.p-button-danger):not([disabled])').click(); ``` **Valid range:** 1000–9999 (4 digits, leading zeros not valid) --- ### 7. Duplicate/Overwrite Dialog When a cart ID **already exists** in the system, a PrimeNG confirm dialog appears. The app has multiple `p-confirmdialog` components registered with different keys. The overwrite one likely uses key `"confirm"` or `"warning-continue"`: ```css /* Active confirm dialogs are appended to body via PrimeNG overlay */ p-confirmdialog[key="confirm"] p-confirmdialog[key="warning-continue"] /* When active, content appears in a .p-dialog-content inside */ ``` **Playwright approach for handling it:** ```javascript // After Tab, check if a confirm dialog appeared: const dialog = page.locator('[role="alertdialog"]:visible'); if (await dialog.isVisible()) { // "Try again" / reject overwrite: await page.locator('[role="alertdialog"] button:has-text("No")').click(); // OR accept overwrite: await page.locator('[role="alertdialog"] button:has-text("Yes")').click(); } ``` --- ### 8. Filter Count / Completion Check ```javascript // The header showing "Need Carts (360)" is a PrimeNG Select: page.locator('#user-filter-header-drop-down') // aria-label attribute contains the current count: // aria-label="Need Carts (360)" // To get the count: const label = await page.locator('#user-filter-header-drop-down').getAttribute('aria-label'); const count = parseInt(label.match(/\((\d+)\)/)?.[1] ?? '0'); // Done when count === 0 ``` --- ### 9. Pagination ```html
Loaded 10 of 10

Rows drop off page 1 as they're filled. // After filling all visible rows on page 1, page 1 goes empty — // the test should wait for new rows to load or navigate to refresh: await page.locator('button[aria-label="First Page"]').click(); // OR just loop on page 1 since rows drop out and are replaced by the next batch ``` --- ### 10. Recommended Playwright Test Algorithm ``` 1. Navigate to URL with user param 2. LOOP while #user-filter-header-drop-down aria-label count > 0: a. Get all visible: input.po-text-cart-id[placeholder="---"] b. If none found on current page → click "Next Page" button c. For each empty input (index 0 only, wait for lock clear between): i. Wait for tr.spot-edit-lock to not be present (lock cleared) ii. Click the input (or use .focus()) iii. Fill with random 4-digit number 1000–9999 iv. Press Tab v. Wait ~500ms vi. CHECK: is #warningSidebar .p-drawer-active visible? → YES (validation error): click Cancel, generate new number, retry vii. Assert aria-label="Need Carts (0)" ``` --- ### 11. Authentication Note The app uses an SSO/refresh token mechanism via `/auth/ssoRefresh`. # Also test Assigning/Unassigning a POC locks/unlocks for User 2

h3. *User 2: Spot Lock Verification*

# *Open a separate Incognito Window* and log in as the second user.
# *Locate the same spot* that User 1 is editing.
# Verify that the spot remains *locked during the entire edit session* for User 1.
# While User 1 keeps the inline editing open for 1 minute, *try to edit the same spot* to confirm that it is locked.
#* You should not be able to make changes while User 1 is editing.
# After User 1 finishes editing and the 15 seconds have passed, *try editing the spot again*.
#* The spot should be unlocked, allowing you to edit after this time.

----

h3. Quick Order Locking (Single Spot)

* User A opens Quick Order:
** The spot should remain locked until editing is complete.
** *Submit All*: Unlocks all spots.
** *Cancel*: Unlocks all spots.

h3. Quick Order Locking (Multi-Spot)

* User A opens Quick Order with multiple spots and *switches between them*:
** Only the spot currently being edited should be locked.
** Two spots may appear locked for User B while waiting for the *SSO refresh* (~15-20 seconds) to unlock the previously selected spot.
** *Submit All*: Unlocks all spots.
** *Cancel*: Unlocks all spots.

h3. In-Line Edit with User B Watching

* User A edits, User B watches:
** The spot should stay locked for User B, unlocking on save or cancel.
** Fields to test:
*** Title
*** POC Assign/Unassign
*** Start/Due/End Date
*** Length
*** Rotation
*** Status
*** Cart ID (validate on save and cancel)

h3. Concurrent In-Line Edits (User A on Spot A, User B on Spot B)

* *Spot A* (User A edits, User B locked):
** Spot should stay locked for User B, unlocking on save or cancel.
** Fields to test:
*** Title
*** POC Assign/Unassign
*** Start/Due/End Date
*** Length
*** Rotation
*** Status
*** Cart ID (validate on save and cancel)
* *Spot B* (User B edits, User A locked):
** Spot should stay locked for User A, unlocking on save or cancel.
** Fields to test (same as Spot A).

9. QO (Quick Order) locks/unlocks spot for other users

Use the following SQL on vSuite TEST to easily verify the access with only the user’s id:
{color:#ff991f}NO NEED TO CHECK RESTRICTED STATIONS ON THIS CARD. {color}

{code:sql}-- Stations the user has access to
SELECT
    u.id,
    CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) AS full_name,
    u.email_address,
    s.official_callletters AS station_call_letters,
    s.id,
    'Allowed' AS station_type
FROM users u
JOIN JSON_TABLE(u.metadata, '$.stations[*]'
      COLUMNS(stationId INT PATH '$')
) AS jt ON TRUE
JOIN vsuite.stations s ON s.id = jt.stationId
WHERE s.ppo_status_code_id = 3 AND u.id = 613574

    CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) AS full_name,
    u.email_address,
    s.official_callletters AS station_call_letters,
    s.id,
    'Restricted' AS station_type

      COLUMNS(stationId INT PATH '$')
) AS rjt ON TRUE
JOIN vsuite.stations s ON s.id = rjt.stationId
WHERE s.ppo_status_code_id = 3 AND u.id = 613574;
{code}

Perform regression testing to confirm date behavior displays, sorts, and functions correctly when firms use different date formats.

This test should validate that:

* *Demo Broadcasting* and *Demo Telecasting* remain set to *m-d-y*
* *All Ace radio markets* remain set to *d-m-y*

Testing should cover order entry, summary view, list-based displays, calendar view, and sorting behavior for all available date-related columns.

*Objective*
Ensure date formatting is displayed correctly per firm setting and that mixed-format firms do not introduce regressions in entry, display, filtering, or sorting.

*Preconditions*

# Demo Broadcasting is configured for *m-d-y*
# Demo Telecasting is configured for *m-d-y*
# All Ace radio markets are configured for *d-m-y*
# Test users have access to the applicable firms and views
# Test data exists with a variety of date values for:
#* Due Date
#* Days
#* Submitted On
#* Start Date
#* End Date

*Scope*
Validate date behavior in the following areas:

* Order Entry Form
* Order Entry Summary View
* List View
* Compact View
* Calendar View
* Sorting in List View
* Sorting in Compact View

*Testing Instructions*

# *Firm Setup Validation*

# Log into each test firm listed above.
## HDash>Firms>Demo Broadcasting > edit pencil
## In main firm fields, check that the Date Format field is set to mm-dd-yy
## HDash>Firms>Demo Telecasting > edit pencil
## In main firm fields, check that the Date Format field is set to mm-dd-yy
## HDash>Firms>Ace Radio> Gippsland > edit pencil

*Expected Result*
Each firm reflects the intended date format and retains that format consistently throughout testing.

----

# *Order Entry Form*

## Email: [imail-test+DemoProdDirector@vcreativeinc.com|mailto:imail-test+DemoProdDirector@vcreativeinc.com]

*Expected Result*

* Date fields display in the correct format for the selected firm
* Date entry is accepted correctly
* No values are swapped, misinterpreted, or reformatted incorrectly after save
* No validation or parsing issues occur due to firm-specific date format

----

# *Order Entry Summary View*

# Open the saved order in summary view for each test firm.
# Review all displayed dates.
# Compare summary values to the values entered on the form.

*Expected Result*

* Summary view displays dates in the correct firm format
* Dates match what was entered and saved
* No date shifts, reversals, or formatting inconsistencies appear between form and summary view

----

# *List View Display*

# Open List View in each test firm.
# Review records containing Due Date, Submitted On, Start Date, and End Date.
# Compare displayed dates across firms using different date formats.

*Expected Result*

* Dates display in the correct format for the active firm
* No column shows a different format than the rest of the firm
* No inconsistent formatting appears between records or columns

----

# *Compact View Display*

# Open Compact View in each test firm.

*Expected Result*

* Dates display in the correct format for the active firm
* Compact View matches the same saved values shown elsewhere in the system

----

# *Calendar View*

# Open Calendar View in each test firm.
# Review records placed on calendar dates.
# Open calendar items where applicable and compare displayed dates to the order.

*Expected Result*

* Calendar placement reflects the correct underlying date
* Displayed dates match the firm format
* No off-by-one-day, parsing, or placement issues occur

----

# *List View Sorting*


For each firm, test sorting in *ascending and descending* order for:

* Due
* Days
* Submitted On
* Start Date
* End Date

Steps:

# Open List View.
# Sort by each date-related option one at a time.
# Review record order carefully.

*Expected Result*

* Sorting is based on actual date value, not text/string value
* Ascending and descending results are correct
* Sorting behaves the same regardless of whether the firm uses m-d-y or d-m-y

----

# *Compact View Sorting*


For each firm, test sorting in *ascending and descending* order for:

* Due
* Days
* Submitted On
* Start Date
* End Date

*Expected Result*

* Sorting is correct and consistent with List View
* No date format setting causes incorrect sort order
* Compact View results align with expected chronological order

*Regression Risks to Watch For*

* Date displays correctly in one view but not another
* Summary view differs from form entry
* Sorting based on displayed text instead of actual date value
* Dates saving as the wrong month/day combination
* Calendar rendering the wrong day
* Cross-firm contamination where one firm’s format affects another

*Pass/Fail Criteria*
*Pass* if:

* All date fields display correctly per firm setting
* Dates save and reload accurately
* All tested views remain consistent
* Sorting works chronologically in both list and compact view
* Calendar behavior matches stored dates

*Fail* if:

* Any date displays in the wrong format

* Calendar placement is wrong
* One firm’s format affects another firm’s behavior

h2. 1. Quick Orders (Highest Priority)

* *Multi-Spot Stress*: Create an order with *25+ spots*. Scroll up and down the list quickly.
** _Goal_: No "stuttering" or lag scrolling.
* *Data Entry*: Select a Station, then immediately try to change a Date or Status field.
** _Goal_: Fields should respond immediately and save correctly.
* *The "Double Open"*: Open a Quick Order, close it, and immediately open a different one.
** _Goal_: The second order must show the correct new data, not the data from the previous one.

IMPORTANT

*If the app starts to feel slow or "heavy":*

# *Do not* refresh the page.
# *Do not* close the browser.
# Immediately notify Josh Schauer so he can check the technical performance data.

h2. 2. Inline Editing (List Views)

* *Rapid Edits*: In the Production Orders list, click into 5 different rows and change their status or a date field back-to-back.
** _Goal_: Each change should save and the "Saving..." indicator should disappear quickly.
* *Date Pickers*: Open a date picker in the list, select a date, and move to the next row immediately.
** _Goal_: The date picker should close automatically and the value should save.
* *Stuck Saving*: Watch for any row that stays in a "Saving" state for more than a few seconds.

h2. 3. Product Selection Page

* *Navigation*: Go to another page and then back to Product Selection several times.
** _Goal_: It should load correctly every time without getting progressively slower.

h2. 4. General Forms & Dropdowns (VForms)

* *Drop-down Speed*: Open a form (like Client Info). Click a drop-down menu and scroll through it.
* *Rapid Toggle*: Open a drop-down and click away to close it 5 times quickly.
** _Goal_: The menu shouldn't "hang" or stay stuck on the screen.

h2. 5. Simple Search Stability

* *Repeated Searches*: Perform 5 searches back-to-back using different terms.
** _Goal_: Results should appear quickly without the app slowing down.

h2. 6. Tasks & Activities Sidebars

* *Panel Interaction*: Open and close the Tasks sidebar 5 times.
** _Goal_: The panel should move smoothly and you should be able to click on "View Details" every time.

h2. 7. SpecAI Features

* *Dismissing*: Verify that the AI panel disappears completely when dismissed and doesn't leave any "ghost" elements or shadows on the screen.

h2. 8. Voice Requests

* *Sequential Entry*: Create three Voice Requests in a row without refreshing.
** _Goal_: All three must appear in the list with their correct info.

h2. 9. Station Contracts

* *Contract Line Edits*: Open a Station Contract and edit a line. Save and verify it updates the screen immediately without a page refresh.

h2. 10. Client Info

* *Data Accuracy*: Open/close the Client Info panel multiple times. Always ensure it shows the data for the _current_ client you clicked.

h2. 11. Extended Idle Test (Memory Tracker)

* *Long-term Session*: Log in as a *Demo Production Director* and leave the page open for several hours (or the whole day) while performing other work.
* *Validation*: This helps us test the new internal memory usage tracker. Check back occasionally to ensure the app hasn't crashed or become unresponsive.

TESTING
The following tests should be performed on the new QA environment. 
The overall goal is assuring that the system accurately locks and unlocks a spot/row when one user has it actively in a state of edit. This means that a ‘watching’ user will see the lockout occur (typically 15 is less seconds on testing environments) and then unlock in similar time when edits are saved or cancelled. 

[vC | QA|https://qa.vcreative.net/]

Using dueling browsers (one regular, one incognito or different browser type)

#  As AE in one browser and Prod Director, Producer, Traffic on second browser
# Find the same order in each browser
# Test opening the order entry, checking that it’s locked for second user
# Close the order without submitting, ensure it unlocks for the other user
# Open same order, make changes and resubmit
# Ensure it unlocks for others
# Open the same order, close the browser for the user that opened the order
# Reopen the closed browser to the same browser setup/user as before
# Ensure the second user still sees the spot as unlocked
# Perform an in-line edit from list view
# Ensure the other user sees the spot locked until editing is saved (may take up to 15-20 sec to get it unlocked)
# Find a spot with an empty cartID and enter a number, then mark as scheduled.
# Verify that you are able to click on editable fields in list view and make changes.
# Ensure that the spot becomes unlocked once changes are saved
# Perform assigning/unassigning a POC ensuring it locks and unlocks
# Try keeping multi-spot editing open during minimum 1 min, switching between lines, then edit a line and submit, ensuring it unlocks once editing is complete
# Try selecting the spot ensuring it locks and unselecting ensuring it unlocks
# Move card to approved and comment {color:#36b37e}*_Passed_* {color}if all good or notify the smoke room if you find issues within the scope of this card

*Test case UPDATED (10/2/2024)*

h3. *User 1: Inline Editing of Spot*

# *Open an Incognito Window* and log in as the first user.
# *Locate the spot* that you need to edit (make sure you have the correct permissions).
# Begin an *inline edit* on the following fields of the spot:
#* Title
#* POC (Point of Contact)
#* Date
#* Status
#* Cart
#* Time
#* Rot%
# *Keep the spot editing open* for a minimum of 1 minute without making any changes.
#* Confirm the spot remains locked for the second user (you will verify with User 2).
# After waiting for 1 minute, *complete the inline edit*.
# Wait an additional *15 seconds after completing the edit* before asking User 2 to check if the spot is unlocked.
# Also test editing from the QO locks/unlocks the spot for User 2
# Also test Assigning/Unassigning a POC locks/unlocks for User 2

h3. *User 2: Spot Lock Verification*

# Verify that the spot remains *locked during the entire edit session* for User 1.
# While User 1 keeps the inline editing open for 1 minute, *try to edit the same spot* to confirm that it is locked.
#* You should not be able to make changes while User 1 is editing.
# After User 1 finishes editing and the 15 seconds have passed, *try editing the spot again*.
#* The spot should be unlocked, allowing you to edit after this time.

----

** The spot should remain locked until editing is complete.

*** Title

*** Status

** Fields to test (same as Spot A).
